submission.natural_language_explanation: This layer-0 head fires on closed-class tokens that mark a constituent boundary and open a new nominal: above all the comma that separates a completed name, date or list item from the next element ('Phoenix,', 'Carpenter,', '1969,', 'Saturday,'), and the article 'the' (and more weakly 'a') that heads a noun phrase after a verb, preposition or conjunction. rival_explanations: Broader function-word reading: the head simply has a large value deviation for frequent closed-class tokens in general, so prepositions and conjunctions ('of', 'in', 'and') and other determiners ('this', 'their', 'his') should fire as strongly as 'the' and ',', and the top snippets only show commas and articles because those are the most frequent such tokens.

Narrower name/date reading: the peaks are driven by the proper-name and date formatting that follows the mark rather than by the comma or article itself, so commas and 'the' outside 'Name, Place', 'Month Day, Year' or appositive constructions should be much weaker, and replacing the following name with a lowercase common noun should remove the peak.

Lookahead reading: at these boundaries the head prepares the content noun or name of the next token (comma -> an upcoming name, 'the' -> an upcoming common noun), so its activity should track the identity of the following token and fall when the following word is a verb or function word even with the comma or 'the' kept unchanged.
